title: [Text Extractor] Captures mirrored screen area (X-axis inversion) when Windows display language is Arabic (RTL)
author: yahyaabohashemstu
summary: Text Extractor likely mixes RTL-mirrored WPF overlay coordinates with left-to-right physical screen capture coordinates, causing right-side selections to capture the left side.

judgment.rationale: The report gives deterministic RTL selection steps, an attached diagnostic archive, and a symptom that maps directly to the overlay-to-physical-capture coordinate boundary.
evidence: Arabic Windows display language plus right-side selection captures the opposite left-side screen area.
A diagnostic ZIP was attached and extracted; no PowerOCR exception explains the symptom as a crash path.
OCROverlay.xaml does not pin FlowDirection to LeftToRight.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize Text Extractor selection coordinates before screen capture
proposed_fixes.root_cause: WPF overlay selection coordinates are converted directly into left-to-right physical CopyFromScreen offsets even when an Arabic session mirrors the overlay coordinate space, so the selected right-side region can map to the opposite side.
plan: Pin the capture overlay and selection canvas to LeftToRight without changing OCR language or localized text behavior.

Centralize DIP-to-physical selection conversion in OCROverlay.xaml.cs, conditionally normalizing RTL X coordinates, clamping to the monitor bounds, and avoiding double correction when the layout pin is sufficient.
Keep ImageMethods screen capture physical-only, add bounds protection, and extend selection coverage with an Arabic RTL sentinel-region regression or an explicitly manual-gated equivalent.
verification: With Windows display language set to Arabic, place distinct sentinel text on both sides of the screen, select the right-side region, and confirm Text Extractor copies the right sentinel rather than the left.
Repeat at 100% and non-100% DPI and, when available, on a secondary monitor.

confidence.rationale: The symptom, missing FlowDirection contract, and direct CopyFromScreen boundary align strongly, but the exact WPF mirroring behavior and whether the XAML pin alone fixes it require RTL reproduction.

issue_context.summary: Text Extractor selection and captured bitmap disagree horizontally when Windows uses an Arabic right-to-left display language: selecting text on the right captures the corresponding left-side area.
known_information: The issue reproduces on Windows 11 with Arabic display language.
The reporter used Preview 0.101.2373.0 from Microsoft Store and attached a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The selected right-side region is mirrored to the left during capture.
No assignee, linked fix, duplicate, or follow-up discussion exists.
inferences: An inherited RTL WPF layout/input transform probably mirrors the overlay coordinate space while Graphics.CopyFromScreen remains left-to-right physical pixels.
The fix should target coordinate normalization, not OCR language or text-order processing.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is reproducible enough for a design. Code inspection identified a single boundary where visual WPF coordinates become physical CopyFromScreen offsets without an explicit LTR/RTL contract.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, assignees, timeline, and attached diagnostic archive reference.
Extracted the diagnostic archive and found PowerOCR/Text Extractor installed with no PowerOCR exception log explaining the symptom.
Inspected OCROverlay.xaml, OCROverlay.xaml.cs, ImageMethods.cs, OcrExtensions.cs references, and PowerOCR UI tests.
Searched duplicates for Text Extractor Arabic/RTL mirrored capture and found no active duplicate beyond this issue.
Created fork mirror issue for the converged design after confirming no existing [Issue 50215] fork issue existed.

information_gaps.information: A controlled RTL reproduction after pinning the overlay direction, including the pre-normalization selection rectangle
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms whether WPF is actually mirroring the selection coordinates and prevents applying both a layout fix and an unnecessary X inversion.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Run the right-side sentinel-text reproduction under Arabic display language at two DPI scales and record the selected rectangle before screen capture.

design.root_cause: Text Extractor uses WPF overlay coordinates from MouseEventArgs.GetPosition and Canvas.GetLeft as if they are already left-to-right physical screen offsets. In an Arabic/right-to-left shell session, WPF can mirror the overlay visual/input coordinate space while Graphics.CopyFromScreen remains absolute left-to-right physical pixels, so a right-side visual selection is passed to the capture API as a left-side physical region.
evidence: Reporter selected a right-side region under Arabic display language and captured text from the opposite side.
OCROverlay.xaml lacks an explicit LeftToRight FlowDirection on the capture surface.
OCROverlay.xaml.cs scales Canvas.GetLeft(selectBorder), Canvas.GetTop(selectBorder), Width, and Height into regionScaled without checking FlowDirection.
ImageMethods.GetRegionAsBitmap adds selectedRegion.Left/Top to screenRectangle.Left/Top and captures via CopyFromScreen.
Extracted diagnostics did not show a PowerOCR exception, making a deterministic coordinate defect more plausible than a crash or OCR failure.

affected_files.purpose: Capture overlay visual tree and inherited layout direction.
Mouse drag selection and conversion to capture rectangle.
Physical screen capture and OCR input bitmap generation.
Text Extractor UI activation and selection regression coverage.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The transparent capture overlay can inherit RTL FlowDirection from the current UI culture/display language.
implementation_steps.change: Pin the capture surface to LeftToRight so visual selection and physical screen capture share the same origin while keeping OCR language and localized menu text independent.
edge_cases: Do not change OCR selected language or RTL text post-processing.
Check the top toolbar/menu still renders acceptably in RTL languages.
tests: Launch Text Extractor under Arabic UI culture and verify right-side drag draws and captures the right-side region.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Mouse-up code multiplies WPF canvas coordinates by DPI and assumes the result is a physical LTR offset.
implementation_steps.change: Extract a helper that converts a visual DIP selection Rect to a clamped physical selection Rectangle; if a remaining RTL FlowDirection is detected, normalize X as screen width minus the visual right/left before capture. Use it for drag, Shift-move, and clicked-word paths.
edge_cases: Clamp negative and overflow values to the overlay bounds.
Preserve the existing small-region clicked-word behavior.
Avoid double-correcting: verify whether the XAML FlowDirection pin alone already prevents RTL mirroring before enabling conditional inversion.
tests: Add helper-level tests for LTR, RTL, high-DPI, and negative monitor-origin cases if the helper can be made internal/static.
Run the UI selection regression in an Arabic Windows session.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The capture helper assumes selectedRegion is valid physical pixels and captures without bounding it to the monitor rectangle.
implementation_steps.change: Keep the helper physical-only, but clamp/intersect selectedRegion to the current screen rectangle dimensions before bitmap allocation and CopyFromScreen so bad conversion cannot capture the wrong monitor area or throw late.
edge_cases: Do not reverse bitmaps or OCR output for RTL languages.
Keep PadImage behavior for tiny captures.
tests: Confirm the same physical rectangle reaches GetRegionAsBitmap for LTR and RTL visual drags.
Repeat capture on a secondary monitor if available.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Existing tests activate Text Extractor and perform generic selection but do not validate RTL coordinate mirroring.
implementation_steps.change: Add a focused RTL/manual-gated regression that displays distinct left and right sentinel text, selects the right region in an Arabic UI session, and asserts the clipboard contains the right sentinel and not the left sentinel.
edge_cases: If OS display language cannot be changed by automation, keep a manual RTL validation checklist until the test lab can supply that environment.
Run at 100 percent and non-100 percent DPI to cover transform scaling.
tests: Build PowerOCR.UITests and run the focused RTL selection test in an Arabic Windows session.
Keep existing DetectTextExtractor and TextSelectionAndClipboard tests passing.

verify: Manual E2E with Windows display language set to Arabic: place distinct text on left and right sides, select the right-side region, and confirm clipboard contains the right-side text.
Repeat at 100 percent DPI, non-100 percent DPI, and on a secondary monitor if available.
risks: Forcing LTR on the overlay can change toolbar/menu placement in RTL UI, but the capture surface needs physical pixel semantics.
If WPF event coordinates become unmirrored after FlowDirection is pinned, an additional inversion helper must not double-correct.
Clamping invalid rectangles can mask conversion mistakes unless tests assert the pre-clamp geometry.
alternatives: Reversing OCR text was rejected because the wrong screen region is captured before OCR.
Changing OCR language selection was rejected because language selection does not control screen coordinates.
Requesting more reporter logs was rejected because the report and code already identify a local coordinate-boundary design path.

non_blocking_notes: Verify the XAML FlowDirection pin first to avoid double-correcting with manual X inversion.
